title: Private deployment: Offline operator fallback contract and network-safe upgrade acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Define the product-level contract and acceptance criteria for performing control-plane and runtime upgrades for Private/VPC deployments that may be offline (air-gapped) or operate under strict egress constraints. This ticket clarifies required operator capabilities, allowed egress surface, artifact provenance checks, staged rollout semantics, monitoring requirements, and explicit rollback guarantees for customers running Redwood Private behind restrictive networks.
acceptance_criteria: Zero-unknown-egress: By default, Private installs must not open outbound connections to unknown endpoints. A canonical allowlist (DNS/IP + port) is defined and documented; any deviation requires a signed customer exception manifest.

Offline artifact provisioning: Customers can provide signed image/artifact bundles (tarball or air-gapped repository snapshot) and a signed manifest. The platform validates signatures and checksums locally before starting any upgrade steps.

Operator fallback channel: When control-plane egress is blocked, a local operator agent (operator-fallback) can accept a signed upgrade bundle over a customer-controlled secure channel (SCP, physical media ingestion, or pre-authorized S3 mirror) and perform a staged rollout per policy.

Staged canary semantics: Upgrades must support a staged canary using node labels or a percentage of replicas. In offline mode, canary is implemented via staggered node rollouts with health gating; automatic rollback triggers if >10% of canary nodes report critical errors within the canary window.

Image provenance and signing: All images and runtime artifacts used in upgrades must include a provenance signature (cosign/Notary or equivalent). The operator verifies signatures against a customer-provided trust root or Redwood public keys when allowed by policy.

Deterministic rollback: A single command (or API call) must rollback a failed upgrade within the maintenance window. Rollback must restore previous images and config and reconcile persisted state so that client-facing SLOs are not degraded beyond agreed thresholds.

KMS and key rotation: For air-gapped installs using customer-managed KMS, the upgrade path must include secure, auditable steps for key rewrap/rotation that do not require network egress. Documentation must list required pre-shared key material and operator steps.
Split-horizon DNS: Upgrades that modify DNS entries must work with split-horizon setups. Acceptance includes a checklist and test verifying no leakage to public DNS during rollout.

Telemetry-lite policy: In offline mode, telemetry sent to Redwood must be opt-in and limited to aggregated health metrics, non-PII hashes, and signed release identifiers. Any telemetry requiring egress must be traceable and reversible by the operator.

Upgrade observability: The console (or customer-facing dashboard) shows per-upgrade progress, per-node health, and a deterministic failure reason code. Logs required for postmortem must be exportable in an air-gapped-friendly format.

SLA for upgrades: For routine supported upgrades initiated via the operator agent in offline mode, success rate must be >= 99% across staged rollouts in internal integration testing. Any regression below 95% triggers a temporary hold and an investigation runbook.
Acceptance test pass: All automated upgrade and rollback tests described in the test_plan must pass in a simulated air-gapped environment before a release is marked GA for offline installs.
notes: Trade-offs: Full zero-egress would limit automated remote support. We allow a documented exception path where the customer explicitly permits a Redwood-managed mirror or signed bundle drop with audit trails.
Decision: Use operator-fallback agent that runs with minimal privileges and can be launched by customers; avoid persistent inbound control plane channels.
Follow-up: PM to coordinate with Security and Eng on a concise signed-manifest schema and cosign integration spec.
Risk: Customer misconfiguration of allowlist could lead to failed upgrades; include validation tooling to detect common firewall misconfigurations pre-upgrade.
migration_steps: 1) Publish signed upgrade bundle and manifest format docs in private-operator README.
2) Build operator-fallback binary with signing verifications and local checksum validation.
3) Add 'offline-upgrade' workflow to Console and CLI that accepts local bundle paths and validates preconditions.
4) Provide sample mirror playbooks (S3 presigned mirror, rsync over bastion, physical media checklist) in onboarding docs.
5) Run certification tests with at least three enterprise customers to validate mirror patterns and rollback timings.
rollback_plan: Rollback command: 'redwood operator rollback --release <previous> --force' must be available to operators and documented for customers.
Data safety: Ensure database migrations in upgrades are reversible or gated behind feature flags; if not reversible, abort upgrade and provide explicit remediation steps.
Timeouts: Rollback must complete within 5 minutes for control-plane components and within the maintenance window for stateful components; if rollback exceeds thresholds, escalate to incident-runbook.
Operator manual fallback: If automated rollback fails, operator manual steps with numbered checklist must exist (stop new pods, restore images, reconcile KV caches, restart ingress).
test_plan: Simulated airgap integration: Run full upgrade and rollback in an isolated lab with no external egress; verify bundle ingestion, signature validation, and staged rollout behavior.
Partition test: Simulate network partition where subset of nodes cannot reach artifact mirror; verify canary failure and automated rollback triggers.
Provenance fuzzing: Introduce corrupted signatures and checksum mismatches; operator must reject bundles and surface precise error codes.
KMS rotation dry-run: Validate offline rewrap sequence using customer-provided key material; verify no secrets are exfiltrated and rotation markers are logged.
Telemetry audit: Confirm telemetry-lite policy emits only aggregated, non-identifying metrics in offline mode and that opt-in telemetry can be revoked post-upgrade.
